brief: The season button is the best thing this town has for a viewer who will not stay: one click and midwinter is 19.6 real seconds away. Nothing tells anybody it is there. It is advertised by a chevron and a pointer cursor, and below 640px it drops into the plate's caption slot as 10px uppercase. Make the sill legibly pressable and say so once, so a first-time viewer who never touches the canvas still learns the year can be moved. There is already ONE invitation in this town (the canvas touch hint at 8 real seconds) — do not add a second thing shouting: sequence them, or extend the one that exists, so a viewer is never being invited to two things at once.
successLooksLike: On a fresh 390px load with nothing clicked, a viewer is told once — in real seconds, on the reading clock, never twice — that the season can be advanced, and the sill element reads as pressable at both 390 and 1400px. Cancelled if they press it first. Silent on ?pause. probes/touch-hint.mjs still passes for the canvas hint, and the two invitations never overlap in time.
avoid: Do not add a second permanent chrome element, a tooltip that follows the pointer, or anything that repeats. Do not hurry it under ?fast — this is a reading speed. Do not regress the 640px caption-slot layout from #26 or the ResizeObserver from #27; the sill borrowing space resizes the picture with no resize event.
